pages.text: Each bond absorbs infrared at its own vibration, $(thing)ν = √(k/μ)/2π$(). The $(item)Infrared Spectrometer$() must scan across the band, narrowly enough to resolve it: a $(item)Structure Card$(). With one in its catalyst slot, the Synthesis Bench knows its target and takes a shorter route.

The $(item)NMR Spectrometer$() listens to nuclei in a superconducting magnet: they resonate at $(thing)f = γB/2π$(). Keep it below 10 K (superfluid helium in its coolant loop) and the field under 22 T, or it quenches. Its readings are worth Insight.
